report.summary: All nine baseline workflow findings are resolved in the candidate by inspection of code, tests and docs, and no regression was found in the diff. WF-1: README Status, docs/verification.md Remaining limits and host.md Scheduling now state that /loop, /goal, timed audit ticks and watcher wakes are not supplied, name the affected playbooks, and keep their stopping conditions; no wake engine was added. WF-2: both published default prompts begin with `$pstack-codex:poteto-mode`; hooks/mode.py adds DOLLAR_MENTION with backtick/quote/indent/blockquote masking, and test_both_published_default_prompts_activate reads the actual plugin.json and openai.yaml strings. WF-3: `--project` no longer defaults to cwd; resolve_identity() requires exactly one recorded context for the session, verifies the state key, and errors loudly when missing or ambiguous; mode_context() prints the authoritative session ID, project, state directory and a shell-quoted command prefix; test_cli_uses_recorded_context_after_working_directory_changes runs the real CLI from another directory and asserts the next hook context shows the selected playbook; the workspace-write denial and narrow --add-dir grant are documented rather than bypassed. WF-4: docs/setup.md, schemas/models.schema.json and scripts/model_config.py define 18 roles (17 upstream labels plus coordinator), four panel roles as nonempty lists, per-backend effort vocabularies, native-only inherit-parent/auto without effort, CLI-only profiles, and partial overrides that never fill defaults; the setup-pstack host notice redirects to that procedure while the upstream body stays byte-identical; the Python validator and the JSON schema agree on every rule I traced. WF-5 through WF-9: continuation text no longer says rematch, companions are path-only in build/host/index/ADAPTATIONS, the `git show origin/main:pstack/<path>` re-read is mapped, the why-investigator packet limitation is stated in verification.md and evidence, and the sanitized sentences are grammatical. Catalog counts in build.py assertions, routing-index rows and ledger match upstream (47/23/23/46). Disclosure is honest: verification.md itself says final re-review is pending and joint approval is absent, effort is unmeasured, reader proof is local git only, Grok is blocked before inference. Remaining issues are P3: activation is recognized only for first-line, space-delimited mentions (a trailing colon or comma defeats it and README does not say so); README Status omits the reader probe and the named wake-dependent list omits unattended Hillclimb and Visual parity loops; schema and Python validator are dual-maintained with only a shallow cross-check; the injected command prefix quotes the `<action>` placeholder. None lets a workflow silently pass an unsupported gate.

findings.location: ACTIVATE lookahead `(?=$|[ \t])`; DOLLAR_MENTION lookahead `(?=$|[^\w:-])`; handle() evaluates only `first_line`
findings.problem: Activation is recognized only when the mention is on the first line and, for the slash form, followed by end/space/tab, or, for the dollar form, followed by anything except a word character, colon or hyphen. Prompts such as `$poteto-mode: fix the bug`, `/poteto-mode: ...`, `/poteto-mode, please`, or a two-paragraph task whose `$poteto-mode` mention is on line 2 load the skill in Codex but create no conversation-local state, so there is no compaction restore and no authoritative identity/prefix in context. host.md's manual `mode activate --project` fallback keeps this from being a silent bypass, but README does not disclose the first-line, space-delimited requirement.
findings.evidence: Regex definitions quoted above; tests/test_mode.py test_both_published_default_prompts_activate and test_documentation_and_similar_names_do_not_activate cover only space-delimited, first-line forms; README 'How it works' says only 'Activate `$pstack-codex:poteto-mode` and describe the outcome you want.'
findings.fix: Extend both lookaheads to `(?=$|[ \t]|[.,;:!?](?:[ \t]|$))`; optionally apply DOLLAR_MENTION to every non-code, non-quoted line of the prompt; add one README sentence stating where the mention must appear.
findings.validation: Add the four prompt forms to tests/test_mode.py asserting active state and full context, keep the negative list passing, re-run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`.

findings.location: Entire file versus scripts/model_config.py constants (SINGLE_ROLES, PANEL_ROLES, BACKEND_EFFORTS, INHERITANCE_ALIASES, PROFILES, BUDGETS)
findings.problem: The published JSON Schema and the runtime validator are two hand-maintained rule sets; the only cross-check is tests/test_model_config.py test_schema_documents_role_and_backend_constraints (18 roles, one panel $ref, claude effort enum, native profile absence). They agree today on every rule I traced, but adding a role, effort token or field to one side will diverge silently and users who validate against the schema may get a different verdict from `models validate`.
findings.evidence: docs/setup.md step 4 tells users both 'reject unknown role names, unknown backends, invalid effort tokens, empty panels and panel/single shape mismatches'; no test exercises the schema with a JSON Schema validator.
findings.fix: Add a test that, when `jsonschema` is importable, validates every fixture in test_model_config.py plus examples/models.astra-claude.json against the schema and asserts accept/reject agreement with validate_model_config (skip cleanly if unavailable); or generate the schema's role/effort enums from model_config constants.
findings.validation: Run the test suite with and without jsonschema installed; mutate one enum on either side and confirm the test fails.

findings.problem: shlex.join quotes the placeholder, so every activation, continuation and compaction context injects `mode '<action>' --session ...`. A model that pastes the prefix literally gets an argparse invalid-choice error (loud, not silent), and the quoting invites confusion on every turn.
findings.evidence: shlex.quote wraps any token containing `<` or `>`; the injected line is asserted only for session/project substrings in tests.
findings.fix: Build the prefix as shlex.join(["python3", str(ROOT / "scripts/pstack.py"), "mode"]) + " <action> " + shlex.join(["--session", state["session"], "--project", state["project"]]).
findings.validation: Assert the continuation context contains 'mode <action> --session' in tests/test_mode.py.

report.approval_scope: Runtime layer of commit 64716ccce5b58e7195d20789aafaf7d9f88c7c61 as a limited alpha: the Claude analysis/reader/writer adapters over the installed-CLI login route with scoped Bash rules for readers and a single cwd-anchored Edit rule for writers; the common launcher's timeout, normal-exit and handled-signal (SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP) lifecycle as tested with real subprocesses; fail-closed model/tool/receipt evidence including retained-but-unaccepted partial output; and Grok gated as unsupported (reader/writer) or blocked-before-inference (analysis) with the uniform receipt schema. What I verified from source: adapter validation, argv construction, stream parsing, evaluate precedence, signal deferral and termination logic, and that the new tests assert the claimed behaviors. What I accept only as parent-observed sanitized evidence consistent with the code, not independently reproduced: that Edit(/**) governs Write and anchors at cwd on the installed Claude Code, that safe mode suppressed the sentinel hook/MCP/instruction in the probe, that the reader ran git log live, and that the exact Grok argv produced a sandbox error rather than an unknown-option error. Approval does NOT cover: Grok inference or any Grok profile as live; gh-authenticated or complete seven-source why investigations; effort as applied reasoning compute; managed-policy customizations under safe mode; Edit(/**) anchoring when cwd is a subdirectory of a larger repository; SIGKILL/hard-kill reconciliation beyond the documented procedure; Bash rule wildcard semantics beyond the forms live-tested (bare-wildcard and :* prefix); or any workflow-scope claim. The 87 Python and 52 Bun test passes are parent-reported; I counted 48 runtime tests by reading and did not run them.
report.summary: All ten baseline runtime findings are resolved at this commit or accurately disclosed, and the diff introduces no regression I could identify. runtime-01: resolve_tools now treats reader and writer with one branch; a reader with Bash(git log:*) yields --tools Read,Glob,Grep,Bash and allow rules without Edit/Write, covered by test_reader_can_run_explicit_scoped_shell_without_edit_tools and a live reader-shell receipt whose init_tools were exactly Bash/Glob/Grep/Read with zero denials; gh and the seven-source why contract remain explicitly unproven in verification.md and evidence limitations. runtime-02/04: _SignalGuard now records the first handled signal instead of raising, _supervise polls at 50 ms and raises ParentSignal at a checkpoint, Popen is skipped if a signal is already pending, and a post-receipt-write check finalizes a late cancellation; tests/test_worker_signals.py sends real SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to a wrapper at seven windows (claim, hash, output_file, popen, process_record, supervise, receipt) and asserts exit 130, matching public and durable interrupted receipts, kill_sent for a TERM-ignoring child, and ProcessLookupError on killpg. runtime-03: invoking-tool timeout, stale spawned records and hard-kill orphans are documented in docs/claude.md, host.md and verification.md. runtime-05: parse_claude_events retains last assistant text as partial_text with partial_unterminated evidence and status stays incomplete (tested). runtime-06: grok main() uses make_error_receipt, unsupported_profile is a STATUSES member with exit 2, build_env rejects XAI_API_KEY and GROK_CLI_CHAT_PROXY_BASE_URL by name and the launcher receives explicit env and auth-policy evidence (tested). runtime-07: the exact seven-deny argv was probed with no unknown-option error. runtime-08: docs now use the :* form for the investigator example but the writer example uses a space-plus-star glob that is not live-tested and will not match a bare command. runtime-09: safe mode was probed with a positive control and the CLI help was captured; effort remains requested-only and is disclosed; the help's admin-policy caveat is not in the docs. runtime-10: writer allow rules are Read, Glob, Grep, Edit(/**) with no bare Write/Edit (tested), and the live probe recorded one denied outside Write with the outside file unchanged. Receipt identity semantics are unchanged and correct: success and requested_model_verified require exited/returncode 0/complete/no error/no parse errors/every assistant model equal to the requested model, auxiliary usage is separated, and unexpected tools, MCP presence, non-none apiKeySource, wrong permission mode and cwd drift fail closed. No workflow silently proceeds past an unsupported gate in this scope. Eight P3 items remain: doc example semantics, nested-cwd anchor unproven, run_dir under cwd not rejected, managed-policy caveat undisclosed, denials not surfaced as warnings, Grok main lacks an internal_error path, minor lifecycle relabel and SIG_IGN edges, and evidence/doc staleness.

findings.location: Profiles section: 'Example writer allowed_tools: ["Bash(python3 -m unittest *)"]' and the sentence claiming both wildcard forms are supported
findings.problem: The space-plus-star glob requires at least one character after the space, so it does not match the bare 'python3 -m unittest' invocation a verifier commonly runs; under dontAsk that produces a permission denial the doc does not warn about. This exact form was never live-tested: the live writer used 'unittest*' and the tests use 'unittest:*'. The support claim cites permission docs I could not check.
findings.evidence: tests/test_claude_worker.py uses 'Bash(python3 -m unittest:*)'; evidence/verification.json claude_writer ran Bash 4 times with permission_denial_count 0 under the bare-wildcard form; is_scoped_bash_rule accepts all three forms without distinguishing them.
findings.fix: Use 'Bash(python3 -m unittest:*)' as the writer example (matches bare and argumented invocations and matches the tests). If the glob form is kept, state that it requires arguments after the space and has not been live-tested.
findings.validation: Doc diff; optionally a low-effort writer probe using the exact example rule that runs bare 'python3 -m unittest' and reports permission_denial_count 0.

findings.location: resolve_tools comment 'CLI-supplied / patterns anchor at the primary working directory' and docs/claude.md 'anchors at the primary launch directory'
findings.problem: The probe shows Edit(/**) permits an in-cwd Write and denies an outside Write, but nothing records whether cwd was a repository root. If Claude Code resolves '/' patterns against the project root derived from the git toplevel rather than the launch cwd, a writer launched in a subdirectory of a monorepo could edit sibling packages, which is exactly the arena/swarm sibling-writer case the scoping is meant to prevent.
findings.evidence: evidence/verification.json repair_verification.writer-scope records inside_changed/outside_unchanged only; no cwd-vs-repo-root detail; docs/claude.md asserts anchoring without a nested-cwd case.
findings.fix: Probe with cwd = a subdirectory of a git repository and an attempted Write to a sibling directory in the same repository; publish the result. If the anchor is the repository root, emit 'Edit(//<realpath cwd>/**)' (absolute form) instead of 'Edit(/**)'.
findings.validation: Sanitized evidence entry showing the sibling-directory Write denied and the file unchanged, or the adapter switched to the absolute form with a unit test.

findings.location: validate_spec (cwd and run_dir checks) and claim_run_dir
findings.problem: Nothing rejects a run_dir located under cwd (or a cwd under run_dir). A writer's Edit(/**) then covers its own attempt directory, so the child could overwrite launch.json, process.json or the stdout.jsonl it is writing to, corrupting or shaping the evidence the receipt is derived from. The README example path is arbitrary, so coordinators may well place attempts under the project.
findings.evidence: validate_spec only checks cwd is a directory and run_dir does not exist; resolve_tools writer allowed includes Edit(/**); artifact files are 0600 but owned by the same user as the child.
findings.fix: In validate_spec, reject when os.path.realpath(run_dir) is inside os.path.realpath(cwd) or vice versa (SpecError before claim), and say so in README/docs/claude.md.
findings.validation: Unit test in tests/test_worker_common.py: spec with run_dir under cwd raises SpecError and leaves no directory; existing tests keep run_dir as a sibling of cwd or under a separate root.

findings.location: Profiles section: 'Safe mode suppresses automatic customizations'
findings.problem: The captured CLI help says admin-managed (policy) settings still apply under --safe-mode. Managed hooks or MCP servers would not be suppressed; the receipt detects MCP presence from init but cannot see hooks at all. The doc states the suppression without this caveat, so an enterprise-managed host could inject behavior the operator believes is disabled.
findings.evidence: Captured help excerpt: 'Admin-managed (policy) settings still apply.'; parse_claude_events checks only init.mcp_servers; the safe-mode probe ran in a scratch project without managed settings.
findings.fix: Add one sentence: managed policy settings (including hooks and MCP servers) still apply under safe mode; MCP presence fails the receipt, hooks are not detectable, so managed hosts need a separate check.

findings.problem: Permission denials are recorded only as a count and tool list; the receipt status stays success and the exit code is 0. A coordinator that gates on exit code or errors will not notice that the worker was blocked from part of its task. The docs tell the parent to inspect the count, but the receipt itself could carry the signal.
findings.evidence: evidence/verification.json repair_verification.writer-scope: status success, permission_denial_count 1, errors []; evaluate never reads permission_denial_count.
findings.fix: When the evidence permission_denial_count is greater than zero, append a warning such as 'permission_denials: N (tools: ...)' to the receipt warnings; keep status unchanged so delivery and acceptance remain separate.
findings.validation: Extend test_provider_failure_incomplete_stream_and_denials_are_distinct to assert the warning text is present for the permission_denial scenario.

findings.problem: Any other exception from run() (for example RuntimeError from run_process on a non-POSIX host, or an unexpected adapter bug) escapes with a traceback and no receipt, unlike claude_worker.main which emits an internal_error receipt. Coordinators reading receipts must special-case the Grok backend again for this path.
findings.evidence: claude_worker.main has 'except Exception' producing make_error_receipt(spec, 'internal_error', ...); grok_worker.main has no equivalent.
findings.fix: Add 'except Exception as error' after the ValueError/OSError clause that prints the traceback to stderr and emits make_error_receipt(spec, 'internal_error', [...]).
findings.validation: Unit test patching grok_worker.run to raise RuntimeError and asserting an internal_error receipt with exit code 1 on stdout.

findings.location: _run_claimed_process 'if guard.requested_signal is not None: lifecycle = "interrupted"'; run_process finally guard.restore(); _SignalGuard.install()
findings.problem: Three small lifecycle edges: (a) a first stop signal that arrives while the timeout termination sequence is running relabels lifecycle 'timeout' as 'interrupted', so the status and errors lose the timeout cause even though the termination record shows the TERM/KILL sequence; (b) a signal arriving after the post-receipt-write check but before guard.restore is recorded and then dropped, so the worker exits 0 with a success receipt despite a stop request; (c) install() replaces an inherited SIG_IGN disposition (for example SIGHUP under nohup-style launch) with a terminating handler, contrary to the convention of leaving ignored signals ignored. None affects child cleanup.
findings.evidence: _supervise returns lifecycle 'timeout' with record term_sent/kill_sent; the following unconditional override sets 'interrupted'; restore() reinstalls previous handlers without acting on a pending requested_signal; install() calls signal.signal for every handled name regardless of previous disposition.
findings.fix: Keep the original lifecycle and add an 'interrupted' error entry when a signal arrives after termination began; in run_process, after restore, record any still-pending signal into the returned receipt's late_parent_signals; skip installing a handler when the previous disposition is SIG_IGN.
findings.validation: Unit tests: timeout child plus SIGTERM during grace asserts status timeout with an interrupted error; SIGHUP set to SIG_IGN before run_process is left ignored.
